name: Caro-Kann Defense
description: A solid answer to 1.e4. Black supports ...d5 with ...c6, develops the light-squared bishop before ...e6, and gets a sound pawn structure.
summary: The Caro-Kann is one of the most reliable defences to 1.e4. It is less sharp than the Sicilian and avoids the French's main problem: Black plays ...c6 and ...d5, gets the light-squared bishop out to f5 or g4, and only then closes the position with ...e6. Black usually gets a healthy structure and fewer weaknesses, at the cost of a little less space early on. This course covers the replies you will meet most often: the Advance, Exchange, Panov–Botvinnik, Classical and Two Knights, plus common sidelines.
keyIdeas: ...c6 then ...d5 challenges e4 without blocking the c8 bishop.
Develop the light-squared bishop (to f5 or g4) before playing ...e6.
Against the Advance, strike at the base of White's pawn chain with ...c5.
When White gets an isolated d-pawn (Panov), blockade it on d5 and trade pieces.
A solid position first, counterplay later: Black rarely needs to hurry.
